newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 6.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 6.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name products and Consumer Trends.
PARIS - Euro RSCG, the advertising agency subsidiary of France's Havas, says it merges two existing agencies to form a single transnational agency covering northern France and Belgium.

PARIS - French television audiences fell sharply in the first quarter of 1997, according to figures from both audience measurement body Mediametrie and Carat, which quantifies the purchase of advertising space. Both bodies find a drop of 1.3 million viewers compared to spring 1996, the sharpest fall since 1992 during the Gulf War. (Liberation)

PARIS - A deal under which France's Infogrames Entertainment is to buy the multimedia activities of Philips Electronics will be signed in the next few days, a purely technical delay, says Bruno Bonnell, chairman of Infogrames. (Reuter)

PARIS - French cable company operator Lyonnaise Cable, a unit of Lyonnaise des Eaux, has chosen the telecoms division of Alcatel Alsthom to supply the first fixed-telephone network to be used over cable television in Europe, Alcatel says. (Reuter)

CANNES - The Cannes film festival is to launch its 50th birthday edition on Wednesday with celebrations slightly muted by reported Chinese censorship and by the stabbing of France's Culture Minister. (Reuter)

LONDON - Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel says a panel of experts decided it was entitled to damages from consortium TML for deficiencies in some rolling stock, but rejected Eurotunnel's demands relating to revenue losses. (Reuter)

PARIS - France's Socialists will review the planned closure of carmaker Renault SA's Belgian plant at Vilvoorde if they win the May 25/June 1 parliamentary elections, their leader Lionel Jospin says. (Reuter)
PARIS - French tobacco group Seita says 2.5 percent of its shares have been transferred to Credit Commercial de France and another 2.5 percent to the Sofinamm group. (Reuter)
